# kulupay init

Initialize KuluPay in your project. This creates a `lib/pay.ts` file with your selected providers and a `kulupay.json` config file.

## Usage

```bash
npx @kulupay/cli init
```

## What It Does

1. Prompts you to select payment providers (Stripe, Chapa, PayPal)
2. Generates `lib/pay.ts` with the correct modular imports
3. Creates `kulupay.json` with provider configuration
4. Installs required npm packages
5. Adds environment variables to `.env.local`

## Generated File

```ts title="lib/pay.ts"
import { kuluPay, createPgPoolDriver } from "@kulupay/kulupay";
import { stripe } from "@kulupay/kulupay/providers/stripe";
import { Pool } from "pg";

const database = createPgPoolDriver(
  new Pool({ connectionString: process.env.DATABASE_URL! }),
);

export const pay = kuluPay({
  database,
  providers: [
    stripe({
      apiKey: process.env.STRIPE_API_KEY!,
      webhookSecret: process.env.STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET,
    }),
  ],
  baseURL: process.env.KULUPAY_URL ?? "http://localhost:3000",
  auth: {
    getSession: async (req) => {
      // Plug in your auth
    },
  },
});
```

## Options

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--config <path>` | Path to kulupay.json (default: `./kulupay.json`) |
| `-y, --yes` | Skip confirmation prompts |
